entries.subject: Siarnaq published convex-model envelope
entries.finding: Denk et al. (2018) and the author’s rendered model figure supply the selected approximate convex envelope. It is volume-normalized to a 19.5 km radius from the roughly 39 ± 6 km thermal diameter. Treating effective thermal diameter as volume diameter and adding symmetric elliptical caps are display assumptions; this does not reproduce the original inversion model.

entries.subject: Original Siarnaq convex inversion mesh
entries.finding: The reviewed author page linked no native OBJ. An analogous author-file URL probe returned HTTP 404; that unsuccessful probe is not proof that the native model is absent. The figure-derived approximation remains explicitly separate.
entries.revisitWhen: A released Siarnaq mesh with model frame, method and reuse documentation can be compared with the approximation.

entries.subject: Siarnaq JWST NIRSpec PRISM spectrum
entries.finding: Belyakov and Brown (2025) presents unresolved 0.7–5.3 micrometre NIRSpec PRISM measurements. They constrain unresolved composition and do not support a surface lens.
entries.revisitWhen: A released interpretable spectrum can support a chart; a registered spatial product would be needed for a surface lens.

entries.subject: Terrain and geology route
entries.finding: No resolved DEM, registered geology or mapped composition product was qualified; model facets do not establish terrain.
entries.revisitWhen: A body-specific registered terrain, geology or composition release can be reviewed.

entries.subject: Cassini ISS Siarnaq light-curve data
entries.finding: The Cassini archive and author’s observation record supply disk-integrated data underlying the shape inference. The documented time-series view remains a candidate; no light-curve chart is selected.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation view is in scope and the original time-series samples are validated for units, cadence and uncertainties.
